learn.rule: An outline is a plan. It has a topic sentence and three details. Then you turn the plan into a paragraph.
learn.ruleEs: Un esquema es un plan. Tiene una oración temática y tres detalles. Luego conviertes el plan en un párrafo.
learn.model: Dogs make friendly pets. They greet you at the door, they love to play, and they keep you active.
learn.notice: The first sentence is the topic sentence. The three details come from the notes in the plan.

items.prompt: Read the notes. Which topic sentence is the best plan for a paragraph?
items.text: Notes: the sun heats puddles. Puddles get smaller. The water goes into the air as vapor.

options.text: Puddles are wet.
The sun is a star.
Puddles dry up when the sun heats the water.

items.why: A good topic sentence covers all the notes. The first choice is too small and the second choice is about something else.
items.whyEs: Una buena oración temática cubre todas las notas. La primera opción es muy pequeña y la segunda trata de otra cosa.

items.prompt: The topic is 'Clouds form when water vapor cools.' Check the notes that can become details.

options.text: Water vapor rises into cool air.
Elephants drink a lot of water.
The vapor turns into tiny drops.
Many drops together make a cloud.
Many kids like to splash in puddles.

items.why: Details in an outline all explain the topic. The cooling vapor, the tiny drops, and the cloud are steps in the same idea.
items.whyEs: Los detalles de un esquema explican el tema. El vapor que se enfría, las gotas y la nube son pasos de la misma idea.

items.prompt: Complete the topic sentence of the outline.
items.model: Water moves around Earth in a cycle.
items.why: The topic sentence must tell the big idea of the plan. Water moves in a cycle: up, into clouds, and back down.
items.whyEs: La oración temática debe decir la idea principal del plan. El agua se mueve en un ciclo: sube, forma nubes y vuelve a bajar.

items.prompt: Put the parts of this water cycle outline in order.
lines: Topic sentence: Water moves around Earth in a cycle.
Detail 1: The sun heats water, and it rises into the air.
Detail 2: The water cools and forms clouds.
Detail 3: Rain or snow falls back to the ground.
items.why: An outline starts with the topic sentence. The details follow in the order the water travels.
items.whyEs: Un esquema empieza con la oración temática. Los detalles siguen el orden en que viaja el agua.

items.prompt: Which sentence turns the note 'gray clouds, heavy with water, rain' into a complete detail?

options.text: Gray clouds rain heavy.
Gray clouds are heavy with water and bring rain.
Clouds, heavy, rain.

items.why: Notes are short word groups. In a paragraph, each note becomes a complete sentence with a who or what and an action.
items.whyEs: Las notas son grupos de palabras cortos. En un párrafo, cada nota se convierte en una oración completa con un sujeto y una acción.

write.prompt: Use the outline to write a paragraph of four sentences. Start with the topic sentence.
write.promptEs: Usa el esquema para escribir un párrafo de cuatro oraciones. Empieza con la oración temática.
write.text: Topic: Seeds grow into plants. Detail 1: seeds need water. Detail 2: seeds need warmth. Detail 3: roots grow down and a stem grows up.

label: I used words from the outline
Usé palabras del esquema
I used a signal word like first, next, or then
Usé una palabra señal como first, next o then

write.model: Seeds grow into plants. First, a seed needs water to wake up. Next, it needs warmth to start growing. Then roots grow down and a stem grows up.

familyTalk.en: Before telling a story at home, name your big idea and three details. Then tell it in order.
familyTalk.es: Antes de contar una historia en casa, digan su idea principal y tres detalles. Luego cuéntenla en orden.

teacherTip.en: Have students circle the key words in the outline before writing, then check them off as they use them.
teacherTip.es: Pide que encierren en un círculo las palabras clave del esquema antes de escribir y que las marquen al usarlas.

sets.title: Maps and Globes Plan
sets.titleEs: Plan de mapas y globos terráqueos

learn.rule: Turn your notes into an outline: one topic sentence, then three details that explain it.
learn.ruleEs: Convierte tus notas en un esquema: una oración temática y tres detalles que la expliquen.
learn.model: A calendar helps us plan. It shows the days of the week, it shows the months, and it reminds us of special days.
learn.notice: The topic sentence tells the big idea. Each detail gives one reason a calendar is helpful.

items.prompt: Read the notes about a classroom. Which topic sentence is the best plan?
items.text: Notes: Ana votes for class jobs. Ben helps choose the class rules. The class picks a story.

options.text: Ben helps choose the class rules.
Our school opens at eight o'clock.
Students help make decisions in our class.

items.why: The best topic sentence covers every note: jobs, rules, and a story are all decisions. The first choice is only one note.
items.whyEs: La mejor oración temática cubre todas las notas: los trabajos, las reglas y un cuento son decisiones. La primera opción es solo una nota.

items.prompt: Which note does not belong in an outline for 'A map is a helpful tool'?

options.text: The key explains the symbols.
The title names the place.
I ate cereal this morning.

items.why: Every note in an outline supports the topic. Breakfast has nothing to do with maps.
items.whyEs: Cada nota de un esquema apoya el tema. El desayuno no tiene nada que ver con los mapas.

items.prompt: The topic is 'Maps use symbols.' Check the notes that can become details.

options.text: A star can show a capital city.
Pizza has cheese on top.
A blue line can show a river.
A small tent can show a campsite.
Our bus comes at seven.

items.why: Good details in an outline are examples of the topic. A star, a blue line, and a tent are all symbols on a map.
items.whyEs: Los buenos detalles de un esquema son ejemplos del tema. Una estrella, una línea azul y una carpa son símbolos en un mapa.

items.prompt: Complete the topic sentence for the map outline.
items.model: A map is a helpful tool for finding places.
items.why: The topic sentence names the big idea of the whole outline. A map is a tool that helps us find places.
items.whyEs: La oración temática nombra la idea principal de todo el esquema. Un mapa es una herramienta que nos ayuda a encontrar lugares.

items.prompt: Put the map outline in order, from the topic sentence to the last detail.
lines: Topic sentence: A map is a helpful tool for finding places.
Detail 1: The title tells which place the map shows.
Detail 2: The key explains what each picture means.
Detail 3: The compass rose shows north, south, east, and west.
items.why: The topic sentence leads the outline. Then the details are numbered so you can write them in order.
items.whyEs: La oración temática encabeza el esquema. Luego los detalles están numerados para escribirlos en orden.

items.prompt: Which sentence turns the note 'compass rose, four directions' into a complete sentence?

options.text: A compass rose four directions.
Compass rose showing directions on.
A compass rose shows four directions.

items.why: A note becomes a sentence when it has a naming part and an action. A compass rose is who, and shows four directions is what it does.
items.whyEs: Una nota se convierte en oración cuando tiene un sujeto y una acción. A compass rose es el sujeto y shows four directions es lo que hace.

write.prompt: Use the outline to write a paragraph of four sentences. Start with the topic sentence.
write.promptEs: Usa el esquema para escribir un párrafo de cuatro oraciones. Empieza con la oración temática.
write.text: Topic: A globe shows the whole Earth. Detail 1: it is round like Earth. Detail 2: blue parts show oceans. Detail 3: you can spin it to find places.

label: I used words from the outline
Usé palabras del esquema
I used a signal word like first, next, or finally
Usé una palabra señal como first, next o finally

write.model: A globe shows the whole Earth. First, it is round like our planet. Next, the blue parts show the oceans. Finally, you can spin it to find places.

familyTalk.en: Pick a place your family knows. Plan a big idea and three details about it, then tell it in order.
familyTalk.es: Escojan un lugar que su familia conozca. Planeen una idea principal y tres detalles, y luego cuéntenlo en orden.

teacherTip.en: Let students compare the outline with the paragraph and point to where each detail became a sentence.
teacherTip.es: Pide que comparen el esquema con el párrafo y señalen dónde cada detalle se convirtió en una oración.

learn.rule: Plan before you write. An outline lists the topic sentence first and then three details in a clear order.
learn.ruleEs: Planea antes de escribir. Un esquema pone primero la oración temática y luego tres detalles en un orden claro.
learn.model: Folktales teach lessons. Characters make choices, they face problems, and they learn something at the end.
learn.notice: The topic sentence is the big idea. The three details are the plan for what comes next.

items.prompt: Read the notes about a story character. Which topic sentence is the best plan?
items.text: Notes: Tia shares her lunch. Tia helps carry bags. Tia says kind words.

options.text: Lunch can be tasty.
Tia shares her lunch.
Tia is a kind friend in the story.

items.why: The best topic sentence fits all the notes. Sharing, helping, and kind words all show that Tia is kind.
items.whyEs: La mejor oración temática encaja con todas las notas. Compartir, ayudar y decir palabras amables muestran que Tia es amable.

items.prompt: Which note does not fit the outline 'Tia is a kind friend'?

options.text: She smiles at new students.
The door is blue.
She listens when others talk.

items.why: Each note in the outline must show the topic. A blue door does not show that Tia is kind.
items.whyEs: Cada nota del esquema debe mostrar el tema. Una puerta azul no muestra que Tia es amable.

items.prompt: The topic is 'The setting of a story tells where and when it happens.' Check the notes that can become details.

options.text: A story might happen in a forest.
Dogs wag their tails when they are happy.
A story might happen long ago.
The setting can be a city, a farm, or a ship.

items.why: Details for this outline are examples of settings. A forest, long ago, and a ship all tell where or when.
items.whyEs: Los detalles de este esquema son ejemplos de escenarios. Un bosque, hace mucho tiempo y un barco dicen dónde o cuándo.

items.prompt: Complete the detail for the middle of the story outline.
parts: In the middle of a story, the characters face a
items.model: In the middle of a story, the characters face a problem.
items.why: The middle of a story is where the problem grows. The word problem is the only choice that fits the story plan.
items.whyEs: El medio de un cuento es donde crece el problema. La palabra problem es la única opción que encaja con el plan del cuento.

items.prompt: Put the story outline in order, from the topic sentence to the last detail.
lines: Topic sentence: Every story has a beginning, a middle, and an end.
Detail 1: The beginning tells who is in the story and where it happens.
Detail 2: The middle shows a problem that the characters face.
Detail 3: The end tells how the problem is solved.
items.why: The topic sentence comes first. The details follow the order of a story: beginning, middle, end.
items.whyEs: La oración temática va primero. Los detalles siguen el orden de un cuento: principio, medio y final.

write.prompt: Use the outline to write a paragraph of four sentences. Start with the topic sentence.
write.promptEs: Usa el esquema para escribir un párrafo de cuatro oraciones. Empieza con la oración temática.
write.text: Topic: Our class pet is a great friend. Detail 1: it is soft and quiet. Detail 2: we feed it every day. Detail 3: it makes us smile.

label: I used words from the outline
Usé palabras del esquema
I used a signal word like first, next, or finally
Usé una palabra señal como first, next o finally

write.model: Our class pet is a great friend. First, it is soft and quiet. Next, we feed it every day. Finally, it makes us smile.

familyTalk.en: Think of a favorite book. Say its big idea and three details from the story.
familyTalk.es: Piensen en un libro favorito. Digan su idea principal y tres detalles del cuento.

teacherTip.en: Model turning one note into a full sentence on the board before students write their own.
teacherTip.es: Muestra en la pizarra cómo convertir una nota en una oración completa antes de que escriban la suya.
